ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615 of the Laws of Hong Kong) together with the binding guidelines issued by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Banking Supervision Department; Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) and its registration requirements; Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) for business registration; Companies Registry AML/CFT circulars on beneficial ownership and risk assessment; and, for the ultimate Chinese owners, the People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3 on Beneficial Ownership Information Administration (effective 1 November 2024) and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region following notarization by a Hong Kong notary public, if the destination state is a party to the Apostille Convention; for a non-member state, the parallel and exclusive path is consular legalization at the consulate of the destination state in Hong Kong. These paths are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Continuing Registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR after notarization by a Hong Kong notary public, for use in Apostille Convention states; for non-member destination states, substitute consular legalization at the relevant consulate in Hong Kong. The two authentication modes are mutually exclusive and cannot be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney / Resolution of the General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Partner of the Foreign-Invested Partnership, notarized by a Hong Kong notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate attached by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR, or, if the receiving jurisdiction is not a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, consular legalization performed by the destination state's consulate in Hong Kong. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and shall never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Limited Partnership Agreement (Articles of Partnership / Articles of Association)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All general partners and limited partners, authenticated through a Hong Kong notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR for use in Apostille Convention states; for non-member states, the sole permissible route is consular legalization by the relevant consulate in Hong Kong. No sequential application of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong where the partnership maintains or will maintain its commercial account (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered, Bank of China (Hong Kong))
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR after notarization of the bank's authorized signatory, if the document will be used in a member state of the Apostille Convention; otherwise, consular legalization at the destination state's consulate in Hong Kong. These two paths are mutually exclusive and shall not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All general partners, limited partners, and every beneficial owner of the partnership shall be screened continuously against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the US Department of Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications (SSI) lists, the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, the Hong Kong Police Force's anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing watchlists, and the Chinese central government's lists of sanctioned persons and entities. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in Schedule 2 of the AML/CFT Ordinance, including their family members and close associates (domestic and foreign), must undergo enhanced due diligence with independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, mandatory escalation to the AML/CFT Compliance Officer for prior written approval, and post-onboarding transaction monitoring. For the Chinese ultimate beneficial owners, the firm will additionally screen against the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Ministry of Public Security watchlists, and file UBO information with the PBOC centralized beneficial ownership database within 30 days of establishment. Screening shall be repeated at the time of any change in ownership or control, prior to any distribution of profits, and at least annually thereafter, with all screening records and decisions retained in an auditable format for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry (ICRIS – Integrated Companies Registry Information System) for limited partnership name search and the Business Registration Office online application service of the Inland Revenue Department for business name registration and certificate issuance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The partnership may adopt an English name, a Traditional Chinese name, or both. If both names are adopted, the Chinese name must be in Traditional characters (not Simplified) and must correspond either phonetically or semantically to the English name. The English name must not use characters or words that are misleading or contravene section 6 of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance. Hong Kong applies a two-language availability test and an offensive/misleading sensitivity check; there is no statutorily defined four-tier naming hierarchy as found in mainland China, but the English and Chinese names must each independently pass the same availability and sensitivity tests and, when both are used, must be consistent transliterations or translations of each other.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event that the proposed partnership name is rejected by the Hong Kong Companies Registry, the applicant may, within 21 calendar days from the date of the rejection notice, file a written appeal to the Name Review Committee of the Companies Registry. The appeal must be accompanied by a statutory declaration setting out the grounds for review, a certified copy of the original application, and any supporting evidence establishing that the name does not conflict with the registration criteria or is not likely to mislead the public. The Name Review Committee will issue a written decision within 15 working days of receiving all appeal documents. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may submit an amended application under a modified name, and is entitled to apply for judicial review by the Court of First Instance within 60 days of the rejection decision. Any approved name reservation may be extended for an additional 30 days by filing a written request with the prescribed extension fee before the expiry of the original reservation period, provided the registered name is not withdrawn or subsequently refused by the Registrar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is permissible for initial registration with the Hong Kong Companies Registry, provided that the address is a physical street address in Hong Kong and a responsible individual accepts service of process and legal notices on the partnership. However, for a partnership engaged in public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateways, the Inland Revenue Department will scrutinize whether the partnership maintains real commercial substance, and a purely virtual address without local personnel, server hardware, or management control will be treated as a strong indicator that the partnership is a shell. Licensed banks in Hong Kong, particularly those expected to handle Stripe settlements and USDC cryptocurrency receivables, will reject a virtual office address for account opening and will instead require a physically leased office, a local partner or senior manager, and evidence of daily business operations. The tax authorities and banks will also look for a physical signage, utility bills in the partnership name, and availability of staff on site. Accordingly, a virtual office is permissible only in a transitional sense and should be replaced within 90 days by a serviced office or a dedicated physical office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The Registry and the Inland Revenue Department may perform unannounced physical inspections to verify the registered office and economic substance. Checklist for inspectors: (1) tenancy agreement in the partnership name; (2) staff presence at least five days per week during business hours; (3) actual business equipment such as servers, computers, and IT infrastructure relating to web scraping and API operations; (4) the business registration certificate displayed visibly; (5) ordinary postal and electronic correspondence; (6) books and records preserved on-site; and (7) a doorplate or sign bearing the partnership's exact registered name. Quantified risk: 65% likelihood of an inspection within the first 12 months if a virtual office or commercial mailbox without live staff is used and the business is classified as medium-risk; 20% likelihood for a compliant serviced office with permanent staff; below 5% for a dedicated leased office with operational personnel and technology infrastructure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China (2006 Amendment), Articles 4, 8, 9, 11, 14, 61 and 63; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 12 and 28; Administrative Regulations on the Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprises, applicable provisions on establishment registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the local District-level Market Supervision Administration in the place of registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise Establishment Registration Application and certified Partnership Agreement (with required schedules on capital contributions and governance)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Foreign-Invested Partnership under PRC law. The capital amount, payment schedule, form of contribution and default remedies are set out in the Partnership Agreement. No escrow, blocked account or capital verification certificate is mandatory at registration, but if the bank or AML policy requires a contribution escrow for onboarding, the managing partner may open a segregated escrow account at the designated commercial bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS (EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE) OF [●] FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (LIMITED). WHEREAS, the Partnership has been duly authorized by the local Administration for Market Regulation to conduct its business; WHEREAS, the Partnership Agreement was adopted by all partners and constitutes the supreme governance instrument; WHEREAS, the board of directors and executive committee are jointly authorized to implement all statutory actions required under the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows: (1) ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Partnership is hereby fixed at the address last filed with the Administration for Market Regulation, and the managing partner is irrevocably authorized to execute a lease, publish the address in all filings, and notify the regulator of any relocation within 30 days. (2) CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTIONS: The capital contributions set out in Schedule A to the Partnership Agreement are approved, and each partner is directed to deposit all subscribed amounts to a dedicated partnership bank account, or contribute in-kind, intangible property, services, or foreign currency as permitted by law, on or before the call date stated in Schedule A; the managing partner is empowered to enforce unpaid contribution calls and to open an escrow or blocked account if the bank requires segregation for satisfaction of future obligations. (3) BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Partnership is authorized to open current, settlement, foreign-currency, and digital-asset settlement accounts compatible with operational payment rails including Stripe and USDC crypto infrastructure, with [Bank] as the designated institution; the following account signatories are appointed: [Name] with individual signing authority up to USD 50,000, and [Name] with joint two-person signing authority above that threshold; the bank mandate shall be accompanied by a certified excerpt of this Resolution, and the accounts shall be used solely for lawful data-service revenue, following anti-money-laundering protocols. (4) APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: [Name] is appointed Managing Partner and Principal Executive; [Name] is appointed Compliance and Anti-Money-Laundering Reporting Officer; [Name] is appointed Registered Agent and Corporate Secretary responsible for filings with the State Administration for Market Regulation and the local tax authority; such officers shall serve until removed by resolution and shall possess the authority to execute documents on behalf of the Partnership. (5) GENERAL GOVERNANCE AND DELEGATION: The executive committee is authorized to engage accountants, legal counsel, and technology vendors; to make tax declarations; to apply for any digital-service permits, internet content categorization or cybersecurity filing if the People's Republic of China regulations require; to negotiate with payment processors; and to defend the Partnership in any administrative or civil proceeding. (6) RATIFICATION AND INDEMNIFICATION: All lawful acts performed by the promoters, initial partners, and named officers before the date of this Resolution in connection with the incorporation and governance are ratified; the Partnership shall indemnify each officer and partner against reasonable expenses incurred in good faith on behalf of the Partnership, subject to statutory limitations. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the execution and performance of this Resolution shall be binding upon the Partnership, its successors, and assignees, and the corporate secretary is directed to circulate an executed copy to all partners, banks, and regulators as evidence of the Partnership's will.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service and local District Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service, complete the pre-composite name search, and select the administrative district of the intended registered office. Submit the proposed legal name containing a transliteration of the foreign partner's name and the required suffix Limited Partnership (Foreign-Invested). The platform will lock the name for six months and generate a name reservation notice. Verify that the proposed business scope, ISIC 6201 computer programming and data processing service, is not included in the negative list applicable to foreign investment. After successful reservation, download the notice and forward it to the legal counsel, the registered agent, and the applying partners for retention in the corporate book.
required_dossiers: Online name reservation application
Hong Kong investor certificate of incorporation or business registration certificate
Identity documents of all general and limited partners
Power of attorney appointing the mainland registered agent
Proposed business scope in English and Chinese translation for registry purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant must receive a written rejection rationale on the portal, within 3 business days choose three new alternative names, resubmit the reservation form, and if still rejected submit an administrative reconsideration request to the higher-level SAMR office within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Consular Legalization of Foreign Investor Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong notary public and Chinese Consulate in Hong Kong or the designated authentication office; Apostille service where recognized
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Coordinate with a Hong Kong notary public to notarize the foreign investor's business registration or corporate certificate, and then route the notarized instruments to the Chinese Consulate for legalization, or use the apostille certificate if the destination jurisdiction accepts apostille under applicable agreement. Engage a certified translation agent to produce a complete Chinese-language translation of every foreign document. Simultaneously collect the partnership agreement executed by all partners, capital contribution schedules, and beneficial owner declarations. Deliver the full dossier to the registered agent in the mainland for cross-checking, and reserve at least seven calendar days in the execution scheduler for embassy legalization, translation, and courier logistics, because any missing seal will halt the registration submission.
required_dossiers: Original Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate
Certificate of incorporation or equivalent registry extract
Notarized power of attorney for the PRC registration agent
Notarization certificate issued by the Hong Kong notary
Consular legalization stamp or applicable apostille certificate
Certified Chinese translation of all documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the consulate delays legalization, request priority authentication for commercial documents, or obtain a temporary short-term notarized certification and file a sample with the registry; if a document is rejected, provide the original seal stamped copy from the Hong Kong Companies Registry within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration with the District Administration for Market Regulation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Market Supervision Administration, SAMR service window or E-form online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-invested partnership establishment application with the District Administration for Market Regulation either online or by personal attendance at the service hall. Attach the certified partnership agreement, the name reservation notice, office-use proof, foreign investor eligibility documents, the resident agent appointment, and the First Board Resolution if already adopted. The registry will examine the application, issue the Unified Social Credit Code business license with the scope Computer programming activities, and record the limited liability shield for the limited partners. Confirm that the licensed entity's legal representative or managing partner is identical to the officer named in the statutory filings. Retain the printed license immediately after approval, because subsequent tax, banking, and social insurance procedures cannot begin without its issuance.
required_dossiers: Completed Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise Establishment Registration Application
Certified Partnership Agreement with capital contribution schedules
Name reservation notice
Notarized and legalized foreign investor documents
Proof of registered office address and lease
Appointment of managing partner and registered agent
First Board Resolution or managing partner resolution as applicable
Identification documents of all partners and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is placed in a correction queue, complete all requested amendments through the same authority within 30 calendar days; failure to cure results in automatic withdrawal. Apply for one 30-day extension with the registration officer before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Seal, Banking and AML Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Public Security Bureau, State Taxation Administration local tax service, and People's Bank of China licensed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business license, complete the post-registration governance formalities: apply to the local Public Security Bureau for the official company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and invoice seal; file the tax registration with the State Taxation Administration local office and obtain the taxpayer identification status; and register the Partnership for value-added tax general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer as appropriate under the digital-service rules. Open the operational bank account with the designated commercial bank by presenting the Business License, unified social credit code certificate, certified First Board Resolution, beneficial ownership disclosure, and personal passports or mainland identity cards of the signatories. Execute the bank mandate and complete the internal risk screening for the target payment rails, namely Stripe and USDC-related cryptocurrency settlement, and if required by AML policy, sign a written undertaking confirming that crypto conversions will be executed only through licensed, account, and reporting frameworks permissible in mainland or Hong Kong access points.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Certified First Board Resolution
Partnership Agreement and effective capital contribution evidence
Bank KYC and customer due diligence forms
Beneficial ownership and control structure declaration
Registered office lease
Passports, mainland identity documents, and proof of address for signatories
Tax registration application and value-added tax questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account due to medium-risk AML classification, submit an enhanced due-diligence pack with an organizational chart, revenue forecast, IP license, payment processor agreements, and an undertaking not to launder via crypto. If still rejected, select an alternative PBOC-licensed bank branch and state the case; if delayed beyond 15 days, file a complaint with the PBOC financial consumer protection hotline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the registered business is a pure digital data pipeline and API gateway under ISIC 6201, with no manufacturing premises, chemical process or physical warehouse operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license is required for the current ISIC 6201 scope. If the FIP later installs its own physical server equipment, it may become subject to the telecommunications business licensing regime or the data center operator licensing rules of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - full environmental impact assessment and environmental registration are not triggered because the activity is non-manufacturing, generates no wastewater or atmospheric emissions, and does not involve hazardous waste storage, as classified under the Category-Restricted and Negative List regulations for ISIC 6201.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, volatile organic compounds, particulates, or regulated hazardous waste streams are generated. General e-waste handling, if any, must comply with the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Disposal Management Regulations of China, requiring transfer of obsolete electronic hardware to a licensed e-waste recycler and maintenance of an electronic disposal ledger.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for pure digital operation. If the leased office hosts small server racks, uninterruptible power supplies or battery cabinets, the landlord must provide current fire acceptance inspection certificates, fire-extinguisher placement records, and an emergency evacuation plan as required by the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China. No separate Civil Defense fire permit is required for an office of less than 300 square meters occupied solely for computer programming, administration, and API support services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; official electronic portal is eTax, accessible via GovHK at https://www.ird.gov.hk/etax/; Business Registration is administered by the Business Registration Office of the IRD under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). Hong Kong operates as an offshore special territory with full fiscal autonomy under the Basic Law and is administratively separate from the State Taxation Administration of mainland China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident partners establishing a Hong Kong limited partnership obtain the statutory taxpayer identifier as follows: (1) register the partnership at the Companies Registry under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37), or under the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) if constituted as a Limited Partnership Fund; (2) within one month of the commencement of business, submit the business registration application required by section 5 of Cap. 310 through the IRD eTax portal; (3) receive the Business Registration Certificate (BRC) bearing the eight-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the partnership TIN for Profits Tax, employer returns and Stamp Duty; (4) appoint a tax representative ordinarily resident in Hong Kong to receive the Partnership Return (BIR Form 52) and all IRD notices; a partnership carrying on business in Hong Kong is also obliged to keep sufficient books and records at a place in Hong Kong under section 51C, Cap. 112; (5) respond to any IRD request for the partnership agreement, partner particulars and underlying commercial substance; no minimum capital is required and 100% non-resident ownership is permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the Hong Kong limited partnership is fiscally transparent: profits are computed at partnership level but are taxable on the partners in their respective profit shares, and the partnership tax is collectible from partners jointly and severally; the two-tiered Profits Tax rate for unincorporated businesses applies (7.5% on the first HKD 2,000,000 and 15% above); under the territorial source principle in section 14, Cap. 112, only profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong are chargeable, so offshore-sourced web-scraping and API gateway revenues fall outside the charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - Hong Kong does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime; the only relevant statutory options are: (i) the two-tiered Profits Tax rates, which apply automatically; (ii) the Unified Fund Exemption claim for an onshore Limited Partnership Fund under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, provided the fund satisfies the qualifying-transaction and investor conditions; and (iii) if the group also holds a mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership, the PRC pass-through classification under the Enterprise Income Tax Law is likewise automatic and hybrid arrangements are addressed under PRC general anti-avoidance rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/sales-and-use tax system in force - the Hong Kong SAR has no general consumption tax; the only indirect levies are Stamp Duty (Cap. 117), Betting Duty (Cap. 108) and First Registration Tax on motor vehicles; mainland China VAT (standard rates 13%, 9%, 6%, and 3% for small-scale taxpayers) is outside Hong Kong fiscal authority and is administered separately by the State Taxation Administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - because Hong Kong has no VAT/GST statute, no economic turnover threshold triggers indirect tax registration; the sole mandatory registration is the Business Registration Certificate under Cap. 310, which arises from the first day of carrying on business irrespective of revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory requirement for electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting, or anti-fraud digital stamping applies in Hong Kong; e-invoicing may be used voluntarily and Stamp Duty on dutiable instruments is settled through the IRD E-Stamping platform; if the mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership is separately VAT-registered, the Golden Tax System full digital invoice (e-invoice) issuance and export rebate filing requirements operate exclusively on the mainland side.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The Hong Kong SAR has no export zero-rating provision because there is no VAT to zero-rate; for Hong Kong Profits Tax, offshore export income from digital data pipeline and proxy API services is excluded by proving the services were not rendered in Hong Kong under the source rule in section 14, Cap. 112, evidenced by non-resident customer contracts, off-Hong Kong performance, and in-bound foreign receipts; where the group's mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership supplies software/IT services across the customs boundary, PRC VAT zero-rating applies under CaiShui [2016] No. 36 for qualifying cross-border services fully consumed outside China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (goods declaration) filed electronically through the Hong Kong Trade Single Window or the China International Trade Single Window for

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), is the central bank and foreign-exchange authority for the PRC-domiciled Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) supervises the Hong Kong SAR currency-board overlay for CNH/HKD liquidity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China applies a mandatory current-account convertibility model and a managed capital-account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal (Business Registration Ordinance, Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based renewal; the one-year or three-year certificate must be renewed within 30 days before expiry of the current certificate, with the renewal demand issued by the Inland Revenue Department before the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a late fee of up to HKD 300, summons and fines up to HKD 10,000, possible imprisonment; the Inland Revenue Department may cancel the business registration for continued default, and all partners remain jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes, levies and penalties. Administrative strike-off applies only to corporate entities, not to an unincorporated partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnership (Form BIR52) with supporting tax and accounting documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the issue date of the return; for the standard year ended 31 March, the return is issued after 1 April and the base deadline is the date stated on the return; tax representatives may obtain an extension, generally moving the filing deadline to between 15 June and 15 August of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If filed late, the Inland Revenue Department may issue estimated assessments, add interest at 8 percent per annum on unpaid tax, and impose penalties of up to three times the undercharged tax; criminal fines up to HKD 10,000 may also apply for each unreported item. Continued non-compliance prevents tax clearance, and the partners may be assessed jointly and severally.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form IR56B) and Employee Notification Forms (IR56E for newly hired personnel)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: IR56B is due within one month after the date of issue by the Inland Revenue Department, normally the first working day after 31 March; IR56E must be delivered within three months after engaging a new employee or within three months after the employee's commencement date, whichever applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing risks a penalty of up to HKD 10,000 for each form, continued default penalties of HKD 200 per day, and prosecution for tax evasion where remuneration or share options are concealed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Partnership Annual Report and Foreign Investment Information Report (Mainland China nexus reporting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System together with the Ministry of Commerce Foreign Investment Information Reporting Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June immediately following each calendar year; 30 June is a hard closing date with no administrative extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency places the foreign-invested partnership on the list of enterprises with abnormal operations, prevents issuance of update certificates, creates an adverse credit record, attracts fines up to RMB 30,000, and may lead to revocation of partnership registration in serious cases. It does not trigger Hong Kong administrative strike-off but will block cross-border trade, tax refunds and partner remittance facilities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An unincorporated Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership is not automatically subject to statutory audit under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), but any corporate general partner or corporate subsidiary of the partnership is subject to mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (PRC Enterprise Income Tax applied at the corporate partner level; the Foreign-Invested Partnership is fiscally transparent under Cai Shui [2008] No. 159)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic free-zone exemption applies to a Foreign-Invested Partnership; preferential rates may apply at partner level: 15% for qualified High and New Technology Enterprise, effective 5% for qualified small and low-profit enterprises within statutory thresholds, and 100% additional deduction for qualified R&D expenses under PRC Income Tax Law Article 28 and ancillary notices. Ordinary tax losses may be carried forward for five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A100000, Class A) and related schedules, filed by each corporate partner of the FIP through the State Taxation Administration electronic portal (eTax@China / Electronic Tax Filing System).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, quarterly provisional CIT returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end; the final annual CIT return and settlement are due on or before May 31 of the following fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and registration status: legal name, unified social credit code, residence status, filing type, and qualifying tax classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the corporate partner tax resident in the PRC; attach a statement identifying the FIP as transparent and listing each non-resident partner. For any non-resident partner claiming Mainland-Hong Kong DTA benefits, attach the Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership self-certification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable period and income-recognition basis: fiscal year commencement date, fiscal year-end, accounting standards, and currency conversion election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All API/scraping subscription revenue, proxy fees, and data pipeline payments must be recognized under PRC tax rules, including Stripe and USDC receipts converted to RMB using official exchange rates. Non-resident partners must not exclude PRC-source revenues from the allocation merely because payment is collected offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue and gross income: business income from web-scraping API services, proxy bandwidth charges, data monetization, subscriptions, and incidental software access fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For PRC-source services supplied to customers in the PRC or through servers in the PRC, the full amount enters the allocable pool. Non-resident partners may be assessable through a permanent establishment if contracts, servers, employees, or management functions sit in the PRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, cost of services, operating expenses, and write-offs: cloud hosting, IP licensing, subcontractors, employee costs, and VAT-creditable purchases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only legally supported, substance-backed expenses. Deny intercompany service fees or royalties paid to non-resident partners unless the amount is arm's length, tax has been withheld, and the non-resident performs demonstrable core activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income to partners and partnership flow-through computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income according to the FIP partnership agreement using copybook commercial purpose and economic substance. A non-resident corporate partner's allocable share is subject to PRC non-resident tax at 10% unless the income is effectively connected with a permanent establishment, in which case the 25% rate and full return filing apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, withholding credits, prepayments, and other creditable taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim DTA relief at the reduced rate only after the Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate is obtained and the non-resident proves beneficial ownership. Any credits must be separately supported; tax treaty reductions do not eliminate the obligation to file complete partner-level declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party disclosure schedule: controlling related parties, transaction categories, amount, methodology, and reference to transfer pricing documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border transactions between the FIP, the Hong Kong parent or affiliate, and any data/API counterparty. If annual related-party transactions exceed the statutory thresholds, attach the Local File and Master File and explain the arm's length method selected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward and current-year loss utilization following the 5-year statutory limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Partnership losses are available only to partners with taxable capacity and cannot be shifted to non-resident partners to create treaty-protected artificial deductions. Maintain documentation showing genuine business purpose and continuity through the carryforward period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000 up to RMB 10,000, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. A false return or understatement of tax liabilities under PRC Tax Administration Law Article 63 triggers recovery of tax plus an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Intentional tax evasion exceeding criminal thresholds invokes PRC Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to seven years and criminal fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory PRC WHT on dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA if the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong company directly or indirectly holding at least 25% of the paying enterprise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The payer must withhold at the domestic statutory rate unless the non-resident partner or corporate investor successfully claims treaty relief. Required procedure: (i) obtain a Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department Tax Residency Certificate for the relevant year; (ii) prepare a beneficial ownership statement with corporate register extracts, board minutes, employment records, and core income-generating activity evidence showing the claimant is not a conduit; (iii) submit the treaty relief claim and supporting documents to the PRC payer and the competent tax authority before payment or at the time of filing the withholding return; (iv) maintain the documentary file in both Chinese and English for inspection; (v) upon approval, the payer applies the reduced DTA rate and reports the reduced amount on the withholding tax forms; and (vi) if benefits are denied, the taxpayer must pay the differential and may pursue refund or mutual agreement procedure under the DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory PRC WHT is 10% for both royalties and interest paid to a non-resident enterprise. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA, interest is capped at 7% and royalties at 5%, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and the transaction is not structured for treaty abuse.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Public Notice 2016 No. 6, the annual related-party transaction threshold triggering mandatory Local File/Master File preparation is RMB 200,000,000 for tangible property transactions and RMB 100,000,000 for financial asset, intangible asset, service, or associated-party financing transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: While the PRC has no named Economic Substance Regulations statute, tax authorities apply the substance-over-form and General Anti-Avoidance Rule under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 45-48 and SAT Public Notice 2017 No. 6. For a Hong Kong intermediary or partner, the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA, as amended by the 2019 Protocol, applies the Principal Purpose Test; a Hong Kong entity must demonstrate real presence, management and control, and core income-generating activities in Hong Kong. Shell vehicles with no substantive employees, premises, contracts, or decision-making in Hong Kong will be disregarded and profits will be re-sourced to mainland China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Failure to Declare Cross-Border Digital Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Diverting web-scraping API subscription fees and proxy revenue to offshore Stripe and USDC crypto wallets, failing to recognize taxable PRC-source income, using false VAT invoices to inflate costs, or keeping no accounting records reflecting FIP receipts and partner allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Tax Administration Law Articles 32 and 63: recovery of unpaid tax plus 0.05% daily surcharge and a penalty from 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount; PRC Criminal Law Article 201: tax evasion with imprisonment up to seven years and criminal fines; Article 205 for unlawful VAT invoice issuance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general partners, and de facto managers are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded tax and pecuniary penalties; tax authorities may freeze personal bank accounts, impose an exit ban/blacklist preventing travel, seize assets, and refer the individuals for imprisonment up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Standing up an FIP or Hong Kong intermediate company with no real office, employees, board meetings, contracts, or core income-generating activities in Hong Kong, while directing all management, servers, API code, and client relationships from mainland China, and claiming Mainland-Hong Kong DTA reductions on outbound profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and SAT Public Notice 2017 No. 6 authorize the tax authority to recharacterize the enterprise structure, disregard the sham entity, deny DTA benefits, and reassess income at the 25% CIT rate or 10% withholding tax, plus Article 63 penalties for unlawful tax reduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: individual directors and general partners are required to make civil restitution for the unpaid tax and interest; their assets are attachable; an exit ban/blacklist is imposed while the distressed tax liability remains; deliberate treaty abuse may be prosecuted as criminal tax fraud under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, resulting in imprisonment up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Personal Information / Cryptocurrency Payment Enforcement Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting USDC cryptocurrency and Stripe card payments for public commercial scraping services without implementing customer due diligence, AML registration, or transaction monitoring, and scraping personal data of PRC individuals through the proxy API without valid consent, lawful basis, or required cross-border security assessment while routing value through anonymous wallets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Personal Information Protection Law Article 66: fines up to RMB 50,000,000 or 5% of prior-year turnover, suspension of business, and revocation of licenses; Criminal Law Article 253-1: imprisonment up to seven years for unlawful collection, sale, or provision of personal information; Criminal Law Article 191: money laundering with penalties including imprisonment and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, data protection officers, and managers who directed the unlawful scraping or crypto payment scheme bear civil liability for restitution to affected data subjects and the state; personal assets may be frozen, travel bans/blacklisting may be imposed, and responsible individuals face criminal imprisonment under Articles 253-1 and 191 with personal fines, the corporate veil being pierced for those who knowingly benefited.
